title: Order the crew build
intro: From idea to a running crew, the way every week-3 project does it.
prompt: Drag into build order, first step on top.

steps.text: Define the people: agents.yaml — role, goal, backstory, llm
Define the work: tasks.yaml — description, expected_output, agent
Attach what the job needs: tools, memory, Pydantic output types
kickoff with template inputs ({sector}) interpolated into the YAML
Read the output/ artifacts and tighten roles, tasks, expected outputs

debrief: People before work, work before wiring, wiring before extras: the YAML pair is the design document, and crew.py stays thin on purpose. The interpolation step is what makes the crew reusable — kickoff({'sector': 'energy'}) reruns the same machine on new input. And the loop closes with review: crews are steered by editing role/goal/backstory text, which is why treating the YAML as the source of truth (not scattered prompt strings) pays compound interest.
